question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose plugin-authored AI safety findings, and if so must emission be available only through a loader-created context that derives identity, trust, and allowed event types from the active plugin record?
rationale: The answer determines a new public plugin SDK and manifest contract, who may assert safety findings, which data is authoritative, and whether the taxonomy belongs in core diagnostics or an optional plugin-owned layer; code review cannot choose that trust policy safely.

options.title: Host-bound core seam
options.body: Approve a narrow core taxonomy but require loader-injected, identity-bound emission and land real host emitters before exporters or dashboards.

options.title: Sponsor the full surface
options.body: Approve the complete plugin API, Gateway store, CLI, and UI direction after defining compatibility, persistence, privacy, and upgrade contracts.

options.title: Keep optional integrations external
options.body: Limit core to generic diagnostic primitives and move detectors, specialized taxonomy, exporters, and dashboards into plugins or ClawHub packages.

recommendation.title: Host-bound core seam
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow core taxonomy but require loader-injected, identity-bound emission and land real host emitters before exporters or dashboards.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects steipete to security-sensitive plugin manifest and public contract review in this ownership area.
